content.title: About
content.content: Fat‑free sour cream is a dairy product made from cream with almost all fat removed. It has a mild tangy flavor, a creamy texture, and a low calorie count, making it a popular substitute for regular sour cream in diet‑friendly cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat‑free sour cream contains about 0.5 % fat, whereas regular sour cream contains 20–30 %.
It is frequently used in sauces, soups, and desserts to add creaminess without extra calories.
Fermentation leaves probiotic cultures in the product, which can benefit gut health.
In the United States it is often labeled as “0 % fat sour cream” or “light sour cream.”
Sour cream can be made from cow’s or goat’s milk, with a slightly different taste profile.

items.title: Low‑calorie option
items.content: Fat‑free sour cream provides roughly 50 kcal per 100 g, allowing it to be used in weight‑management plans without adding many calories.

items.title: Good source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and teeth health; 100 g of the product supplies about 120 mg of calcium.

items.title: Contains probiotics
items.content: The fermentation process retains live bacterial cultures that may help maintain a healthy intestinal microbiome.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Very low fat content
items.content: Minimal fat makes it suitable for people monitoring cholesterol intake.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Individuals with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consuming sour cream.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey proteins should avoid the product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; those limiting sodium should check the label.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Fat‑free sour cream can be stirred into sauces, dressings, soups, casseroles, and desserts. It pairs well with berries, fruits, herbs, and spices. For a thicker consistency, whip it with a mixer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sour cream refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original container. Once opened, use within 5–7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑smell, discoloration, or mold.
